the class of homeomorphims $\mathcal{H}$, between two domains in metric spaces, is the largest class of homeomoprhisms that allows continuous extensions to the closures of domains and homeomorphic extensions to prime end boundaries, provided the domains satisfy certain conditions.

we have established a prime ends theory for homeomorphisms in a very wide class of metric spaces, including Euclidean and metric spaces with a cone-like structure, and that this theory provides a new and useful tool in the study of mappings between such spaces, in particular, in the study of their boundary behavior.

the class $\mathcal F$ of homeomorphims between domains in metric space is a natural extension of the classical class of quasisymmetric mappings, which in particular contains all quasisymmetric, bi-Lipschtz, and (quasi-)conformal mappings.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the inner diameter distance and the bounded turning condition are natural conditions for defining and studying mappings between metric domains and for their continuous and homeomorphic boundary extensions.

, under the bounded turning condition and the structure of the prime end boundary, the class $\mathcal F$ of homeomorphims between domains in metric space contains (quasi-)conformal, quasiconformally approximable and quasisymmetric homeomorphisms.
, in contrast to the classical case in $\mathbb{R}^n$ and $\mathbb{C}$, the prime ends theory in general metric spaces is a powerful tool for the study of mappings and their extensions.
